Temerity

tuh-MER-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Temerity is excessive or reckless boldness; audacity.

It took a certain temerity for the substitute teacher to rearrange the seating chart on her very first day.

Worked Example

Reporters were stunned by the intern's temerity when she stood up and asked the CEO, in front of the entire press corps, why he had laid off a thousand workers the same week he received a bonus.

Temerity always implies a boldness that oversteps -- it's daring that borders on rude, foolish, or reckless.

How Temerity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

audacity

audacity: a willingness to take bold risks, often shockingly so

impudence

impudence: bold, disrespectful behavior

Antonyms

timidity

timidity: a lack of courage or confidence

caution

caution: careful attention to avoiding risk

How Strong Is It? — confidence → recklessness → temerity

confidence vs. temerity

confidence vs. temerity: Confidence is simply a healthy trust in one's own abilities, without the reckless overstepping of temerity.

recklessness vs. temerity

recklessness vs. temerity: Recklessness is an even more extreme, careless disregard for danger or consequences than ordinary temerity.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of temerity.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — temer-

root — temer-: rashly, blindly, by chance (Latin temere)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Temerity comes from Latin temere ('rashly, blindly') plus -ity ('state of') -- 'the state of acting rashly.' Temere itself never became its own everyday English word.

Use the root in a new word: temerarious

Use the root in a new word: temerarious: Old adventure novels sometimes describe a temerarious knight who charges into battle without a second thought.

Word Building

Word Choice

Temerity almost always describes boldness that shocks or oversteps -- it carries a hint of disapproval, unlike a purely admiring word such as courage.
